question:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.
(A) further that further treatment
(B) useless
(C) the doctor concluded
(D) would be
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. CADB.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correctly arranged sentence reads: "The doctor concluded further that further treatment would be useless."

• Sentence part (C) "the doctor concluded" must come first, since it introduces the subject and main verb of the sentence.

• Part (A) "further that further treatment" follows the verb "concluded", using "further" as an adverb (meaning "moreover/in addition") that introduces the noun clause beginning with "that".

• Parts (D) "would be" and (B) "useless" complete the noun clause, giving the logical sequence: concluded → further that further treatment → would be → useless.

• Hence the correct order is C-A-D-B.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: BDCA disturbs the logical sequence by placing "useless" before the subject and verb, producing a meaningless order.

• Option 3: CBAD places "useless" directly after "the doctor concluded", which breaks the noun clause and is grammatically unacceptable.

• Option 4: BCAD begins with "useless", which cannot stand as the opening part of the sentence since it has no subject or verb before it.

NOTE

• In para-jumble questions, always locate the part containing the subject + main verb first — it almost always opens the sentence.

• Watch for adverbs like "further", "however", "therefore" — they usually connect two ideas and cannot begin a sentence unless deliberately used for emphasis.

• Practise identifying noun clauses introduced by "that", as they are a recurring feature of SSC sentence-rearrangement questions.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym for the underlined word in the given sentence.
We cannot achieve success until these antiquated policies are not amended.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Outdated.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Antiquated" means old-fashioned, obsolete, or no longer in use/useful. (पुराना/अप्रचलित)
◦ Example: The factory still runs on antiquated machinery that frequently breaks down.

• "Outdated" carries the same sense of being old and no longer current or useful, making it the closest synonym.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "Current" (वर्तमान) means belonging to the present time — this is nearly opposite in meaning to "antiquated".

• Option 3: "New" (नया) means recently made or introduced — again opposite in sense to "antiquated".

• Option 4: "Updated" (अद्यतन) means brought up to date — this too is the opposite of "antiquated", not a synonym.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "antiquated": archaic, obsolete, old-fashioned, outmoded, dated.

• Antonyms of "antiquated": modern, current, contemporary, up-to-date.

• Do not confuse "antiquated" (old, outdated) with "antique" (an old and valuable object) — the two are related but used differently in a sentence.

question:
Select the correct spelling of the underlined word.
It would be proodent to wait for some more time before selling off the property.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. prudent.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "Prudent", meaning acting with or showing care and thought for the future; sensible and cautious.
◦ Example: It is prudent to save a portion of your income every month.

• Spelling key: PRU + DENT. Remember it has only one vowel sound after "pr" — "u", followed directly by "dent". There is no "o" anywhere in the correct spelling.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "proudent" — incorrect; an extra "o" has been wrongly inserted before "u".

• Option 3: "prodent" — incorrect; the "u" has been dropped and wrongly replaced, giving "pro" instead of "pru".

• Option 4: "proodant" — incorrect; it wrongly uses "oo" instead of "u" and ends in "-ant" instead of "-ent".

NOTE

• Related word forms: prudence (noun), prudently (adverb), imprudent (antonym).

• Do not confuse "prudent" (careful/wise) with "prudish" (excessively modest or proper about sexual matters) — they are unrelated in meaning despite the similar spelling.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
No sooner had I finished my final exam that my friends invited me to join them on a trip to Europe.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. than my friends invited.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rule — Correlative conjunction: "No sooner" is always paired with "than", never with "that", "then" or "when".
◦ Structure: No sooner + had + subject + past participle + than + subject + simple past verb.

• Applying the rule: "No sooner had I finished my final exam" must be completed with "than my friends invited me...", giving the correct sentence — "No sooner had I finished my final exam than my friends invited me to join them on a trip to Europe."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "then my friends invited" is incorrect because "then" is an adverb of time and cannot correlate with "no sooner".

• Option 3: "that my friend invited" is incorrect for the same reason — "that" cannot follow "no sooner"; additionally it wrongly changes "friends" to the singular "friend".

• Option 4: "when my friends invited" is incorrect because "when" cannot be used to complete the "no sooner..." construction.

NOTE

• Other fixed correlative pairs frequently tested by SSC: "scarcely/hardly...when", "not only...but also", "as...as", "such...that", "so...that".

• "No sooner" and "hardly/scarcely" trigger inversion of the auxiliary and subject when placed at the start of a sentence, e.g. "No sooner had he arrived than it started raining."

question:
The following sentence has been divided into four parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options.
The rich / should / help / poor.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. poor.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rule: When an adjective like "rich" or "poor" is preceded by the definite article "the", it functions as a plural common noun referring to the whole class of people ("the rich" = rich people, "the poor" = poor people).

• In the given sentence, "the rich" (subject) is correctly preceded by "the", but "poor" (object) is missing its required article "the".

• The corrected sentence should read: "The rich should help the poor."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "help" is correct as it is — a simple present base-form verb, correctly used after the modal "should".

• Option 2: "should" is correct as it is — a modal verb correctly expressing obligation/duty.

• Option 4: "The rich" is correct as it is — "the" is correctly placed before the adjective "rich" to denote the class of rich people.

NOTE

• The article "the" is used before an adjective to denote an entire class of persons: the rich, the poor, the young, the old, the blind, the deaf, the disabled, the wealthy.

• Such nouns are always treated as plural and take a plural verb, e.g. "The poor are struggling with inflation."

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.
The bell is rung by the peon.
option_3: The peon has rang the bell.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. The peon rings the bell.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence "The bell is rung by the peon" is in the Passive Voice, Simple Present Tense (Subject + is/am/are + V3 + by + agent).

• Rule — Simple Present Tense:
◦ Passive: Object + is/am/are + V3 + by + Subject
◦ Active: Subject + V1/V5 + Object

• Applying the rule: the agent "the peon" becomes the subject; the past participle "rung" is converted to the present-tense verb "rings" (V5, since "peon" is third person singular); and "the bell" becomes the object.
◦ Active: The peon rings the bell.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "The peon ranged the bell" is incorrect because "ranged" is not a form of the verb "ring" in this context ("ranged" is the past tense of "range", an unrelated verb) and it wrongly uses the past tense.

• Option 3: "The peon has rang the bell" is incorrect because the present perfect tense requires the past participle "rung", not the past-tense form "rang"; it also does not match the tense of the given passive sentence.

• Option 4: "The peon rang the bell" is incorrect because "rang" is the Simple Past form, whereas the given sentence is in the Simple Present tense.

NOTE

• The verb "ring" is irregular: ring – rang – rung. Do not confuse it with the regular verb "range – ranged – ranged".

• Remember the three-step check for tense conversion: identify the tense of the passive sentence first, then apply the matching active-voice formula for that same tense.

question:
Select the option with the correct spellings to replace the underlined words in the given sentence.
There was an anouncement by the director of the company that grabed the attention of all the employees.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. announcement; grabbed.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling of the first word is "Announcement" — a public statement or declaration.
◦ Spelling key: AN + NOUNCE + MENT — note the double "n" (an-nounce) which is often missed.

• The correct spelling of the second word is "Grabbed" — the past tense of "grab".
◦ Spelling key: since "grab" ends in a single stressed vowel + consonant, the final consonant "b" is doubled before adding "-ed" (grab → grabbed).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "announcement; grabed" — the first word is correct, but "grabed" is incorrect as it fails to double the final consonant "b".

• Option 3: "anoucement; grabbed" — "grabbed" is correct, but "anoucement" is incorrect as it is missing the double "n".

• Option 4: "anounsement; grebbed" — both words are incorrect: "anounsement" wrongly uses "s" instead of "c" and is missing a letter, and "grebbed" wrongly uses "e" instead of "a".

NOTE

• Doubling rule: A one-syllable verb ending in a single vowel + single consonant doubles the final consonant before "-ing"/"-ed" — e.g. stop → stopped, plan → planned, grab → grabbed.

• Related word: "announce" (verb), "announcer" (noun, a person who announces).

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom for the underlined words in the given sentence.
Ritika had a narrow escape as she was driving recklessly on the highway.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. close shave.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "Close shave" means a narrow escape from danger or an accident. (बाल-बाल बचना)
◦ Example: The car swerved just in time — it was a close shave for the pedestrians.

• Both "narrow escape" and "close shave" convey the same idea of barely avoiding harm, making it the correct match.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: To come in handy (काम आना): To prove useful, especially unexpectedly.
◦ Example: This spare key came in handy when I lost my own.

• Option 2: To cut both ends (दोनों तरफ से नुकसान होना): A situation that has drawbacks or disadvantages on either side.

• Option 3: To cock a snook (मुंह चिढ़ाना): To show open contempt or disrespect for someone/something.

NOTE

• Other idioms meaning "narrow escape": "to have a narrow shave", "to escape by the skin of one's teeth", "to have a hair's breadth escape".

• Do not confuse "close shave" (narrow escape) with "close call", which is a near-synonym also used for a risky situation that ends well.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.
Exceptionally clever or talented
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Ingenious.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Ingenious" means exceptionally clever, inventive, or skilful, especially at devising or improvising new ideas or things. (अत्यंत बुद्धिमान/प्रतिभाशाली)
◦ Example: The engineer came up with an ingenious solution to the water shortage.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Indigenous" (देशज/स्थानीय) means originating or occurring naturally in a particular place; native.

• Option 2: "Studious" (अध्ययनशील) means devoted to or diligent in the study of something.

• Option 3: "Assiduous" (परिश्रमी) means showing great care, attention, and diligence/persistence.

NOTE

• Do not confuse "ingenious" (clever, inventive) with the similarly spelled "ingenuous" (innocent, honest, and straightforward), which is a common SSC trap.

• Other one-word substitutes for cleverness: shrewd, astute, sagacious, resourceful.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
It is nothing but pride.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. nothing else.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rule: The fixed idiomatic construction "nothing else but" is used to emphatically state that something is only and exactly one thing, i.e., "nothing other than".

• Substituting "nothing" with "nothing else" gives the grammatically correct and idiomatically natural sentence: "It is nothing else but pride.", meaning it is only pride and nothing other than that.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "nothing ever" is incorrect because "ever" relates to time (at any time) and does not fit meaningfully with "but pride" here.

• Option 3: "nothing seldom" is incorrect and grammatically faulty — "seldom" (rarely) cannot logically combine with "nothing" in this construction.

• Option 4: "nothing so" is incorrect because "so" needs a following adjective/adverb (e.g. "nothing so good") and cannot stand alone before "but pride".

NOTE

• The phrase "nothing but" itself already means "only"; "nothing else but" is a strengthened, equally acceptable idiomatic variant frequently tested by SSC.

• Similar restrictive constructions: "none other than", "no one but", "nothing short of".

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence.
The doctors say that majority of the people who attended the fest are ill due to eating of adulterated food.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. contaminated.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Adulterated" means made impure or inferior by adding another substance, typically to increase the amount produced or to reduce the cost. (मिलावटी/दूषित)
◦ Example: The vendor was fined for selling adulterated milk.

• "Contaminated" means made impure by exposure to or contact with a polluting or poisonous substance, which closely matches the meaning of "adulterated" as used here.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "spicy" (मसालेदार) means having a strong, pungent flavour — unrelated to impurity.

• Option 2: "lascivious" (कामुक) means feeling or expressing sexual desire — completely unrelated in meaning.

• Option 4: "damp" (नम) means slightly wet — unrelated to the idea of impurity or mixing with harmful substances.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "adulterated": impure, tainted, polluted, debased, corrupted.

• Antonyms of "adulterated": pure, unadulterated, genuine, wholesome.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.
Worn
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Dilapidated.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Worn" (as an adjective) means damaged or shabby through long or hard use; in poor condition. (जर्जर/घिसा-पिटा)
◦ Example: The worn carpet needed to be replaced.

• "Dilapidated" means in a state of disrepair or ruin as a result of age or neglect — this closely matches the sense of "worn" used here.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Dilemma" (दुविधा) means a situation requiring a choice between equally undesirable alternatives — unrelated in meaning.

• Option 2: "Energetic" (ऊर्जावान) means showing or involving great activity or vitality — nearly opposite to "worn" (worn out/tired or shabby).

• Option 4: "Diminutive" (छोटा) means extremely or unusually small — unrelated to the sense of "worn".

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "worn" (in the sense of shabby/damaged): shabby, threadbare, tattered, ragged, decrepit.

• "Worn" can also mean "tired/exhausted" (as in "worn out"), in which case synonyms would be: fatigued, weary, drained.

question:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.
A. before the movie starts
B. should be there
C. at least fifteen minutes
D. the theater management recommends
E. the audience
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. DEBCA.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correctly arranged sentence reads: "The theater management recommends the audience should be there at least fifteen minutes before the movie starts."

• Part (D) "the theater management recommends" must open the sentence, as it supplies the subject and the main verb.

• Part (E) "the audience" logically follows, functioning as the subject of the noun clause that "recommends" introduces.

• Parts (B) "should be there", (C) "at least fifteen minutes", and (A) "before the movie starts" follow in that order to complete the recommendation logically — what should happen, how long before, and before which event.

• Hence the correct order is D-E-B-C-A.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: AEDCB wrongly starts with "before the movie starts", which cannot open the sentence as it has no preceding subject/clause to attach to.

• Option 3: EBCAD wrongly places the subject "the audience" at the very start without the introductory clause "the theater management recommends", making the sentence incomplete and illogical.

• Option 4: BDCEA disrupts the sentence entirely by opening with "should be there", which has no stated subject at that point.

NOTE

• In sentences involving a recommendation/suggestion ("recommends that..."), the pattern is typically: subject + recommends + (that) + subject + subjunctive/modal verb + rest of clause.

• Always identify the independent clause (subject + main verb) first when rearranging jumbled parts — it anchors the rest of the sentence.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word from the following sentence.
Magical
The stories of The Arabian Nights are enchanting, interesting, vivacious, and natural.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. enchanting.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Magical" means having qualities of enchantment or sorcery; producing a strange and delightful sense of enchantment. (जादुई/मोहक)
◦ Example: The magical performance left the audience spellbound.

• "Enchanting" means delightfully charming or attractive, in a way that seems magical — this is the closest match among the given words.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "interesting" (रोचक) means arousing curiosity or attention — pleasant, but does not carry the sense of enchantment/magic.

• Option 3: "natural" (स्वाभाविक) means existing in or caused by nature; not artificial — unrelated to "magical".

• Option 4: "vivacious" (जीवंत) means attractively lively and animated (usually describing a person) — unrelated to "magical".

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "magical": enchanted, spellbinding, bewitching, mystical, wondrous.

• Be careful in "synonym from a sentence" questions — pick the option whose core meaning matches the given word most closely, not merely a word that also sounds positive.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word ‘Regularity’ from the given sentence.
The doctor’s examination revealed a significant abnormality in the patient’s cardiovascular system.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Abnormality.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Regularity" means the quality of occurring or being done at regular, evenly spaced intervals, or the state of conforming to a standard or rule. (नियमितता)
◦ Example: The committee meets with great regularity every Monday.

• "Abnormality" means a deviation from what is normal or usual, especially in a way that is undesirable — this is directly opposite to "regularity" (which implies conformity to the normal/expected pattern).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Examination" (जांच) means a detailed inspection or study — unrelated in meaning to "regularity".

• Option 3: "Significant" (महत्वपूर्ण) means important or noteworthy — unrelated to "regularity".

• Option 4: "Revealed" (उजागर किया) is the past tense of "reveal", meaning to make known — unrelated to "regularity".

NOTE

• Other antonyms of "regularity": irregularity, inconsistency, unevenness, disorder.

• Other synonyms of "regularity": constancy, uniformity, punctuality, steadiness.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.
The character and atmosphere of a place
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Ambience.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Ambience" means the character and atmosphere of a place. (वातावरण/माहौल)
◦ Example: The restaurant is known for its cosy, relaxed ambience.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Haven" (शरणस्थल) means a place of safety or refuge.

• Option 2: "Cartography" (मानचित्रकला) means the science or practice of drawing maps.

• Option 3: "Ligament" (स्नायुबंधन) means a short band of tough, flexible fibrous tissue connecting bones or cartilage at a joint.

NOTE

• Other one-word substitutes related to places/atmosphere: "Milieu" (a person's social environment), "Locale" (a place where something happens), "Sanctuary" (a place of refuge or safety).

question:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.
(P) the research paper analyses
(Q) the relationship between diet and
(R) disease and the importance of
(S) exercise in maintaining good health
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. PQRS.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correctly arranged sentence reads: "The research paper analyses the relationship between diet and disease and the importance of exercise in maintaining good health."

• Part (P) "the research paper analyses" must open the sentence, as it contains the subject and main verb.

• Part (Q) "the relationship between diet and" logically follows as the object of "analyses", and is left incomplete at "and", requiring a continuation.

• Part (R) "disease and the importance of" correctly completes the phrase begun in (Q) — "the relationship between diet and disease" — and introduces a second item, "the importance of".

• Part (S) "exercise in maintaining good health" completes the sentence logically, following "the importance of".

• Hence the correct order is P-Q-R-S.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: PRQS breaks the phrase "the relationship between diet and disease" apart by inserting "disease and the importance of" too early, producing an illogical sequence.

• Option 2: QPRS wrongly starts with "the relationship between diet and", which has no subject or verb before it and cannot open the sentence.

• Option 3: PQSR wrongly places (S) before (R), breaking the logical link between "diet and disease" and disrupting the phrase "the importance of exercise".

NOTE

• When rearranging jumbled parts, watch for words like "and" at the end of a segment — they signal that the segment is incomplete and needs a specific continuation.

• Always find the segment with the subject and finite verb first (here, "the research paper analyses") — it anchors the whole sentence.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence.
The deteriorated building was declared unsafe for the inmates.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. dilapidated.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Deteriorated" means become progressively worse in condition or quality. (क्षतिग्रस्त/जर्जर हो जाना)
◦ Example: The old palace had deteriorated badly over the decades of neglect.

• "Dilapidated" means in a state of disrepair or ruin, especially as a result of age or neglect — a close synonym describing a building in worsened, unsafe condition.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "dissipated" (क्षीण/तितर-बितर) means wasted or squandered, or scattered/dispersed — unrelated to physical decay of a structure.

• Option 3: "meliorated" (सुधरा हुआ) means made or become better; improved — this is actually opposite to "deteriorated".

• Option 4: "reprobated" relates to "reprobate" — to disapprove of or condemn (a person/conduct as morally wrong) — unrelated to the physical state of a building.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "deteriorated": worsened, degenerated, declined, decayed.

• Antonym of "deteriorated": improved, ameliorated, meliorated — note how "meliorate" (to improve) is a near-opposite trap frequently placed alongside "deteriorate" in SSC options.

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom for the underlined segment in the given sentence.
The new entrant in the class felt uncomfortable as all were unfamiliar to him.
option_4: Buried his head in the sand
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Was fish out of water.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "Fish out of water" means to feel awkward or uncomfortable because one is in unfamiliar surroundings or an unsuitable situation. (अनजान माहौल में असहज महसूस करना)
◦ Example: At the formal dinner, he felt like a fish out of water in his casual clothes.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: To leave someone out in the cold (उपेक्षित करना): To deliberately exclude someone from an activity or from receiving some benefit.

• Option 2: Not to give a fig (परवाह न करना): To not care at all about something.

• Option 4: To bury one's head in the sand (सच्चाई से मुंह मोड़ना): To refuse to acknowledge an unpleasant reality or problem.

NOTE

• Other idioms describing discomfort/unfamiliarity: "to feel like a square peg in a round hole" (to feel out of place), "to be at sea" (to be confused/lost).

• Do not confuse "fish out of water" (feeling awkward in a new setting) with "a big fish in a small pond" (an important person in a small/limited environment).

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.
Ramya laughed at me.
option_1: I am laughed at by Ramya.
option_2: I were laugh at by Ramya.
option_3: I was laughed at by Ramya.
option_4: I shall laugh at by Ramya.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. I was laughed at by Ramya.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The given sentence "Ramya laughed at me" is in the Simple Past Tense with the phrasal/prepositional verb "laugh at".

• Rule — Simple Past Tense (with phrasal verb):
◦ Active: Subject + V2 + Object
◦ Passive: Object + was/were + V3 + preposition + by + Subject

• Applying the rule: the object "me" becomes the subject "I"; since "I" is singular, the auxiliary used is "was"; "laughed" becomes its past participle "laughed" (unchanged, being a regular verb); the preposition "at" (part of the phrasal verb) must be retained immediately after the verb; and "Ramya" becomes the agent with "by".
◦ Passive: I was laughed at by Ramya.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "I am laughed at by Ramya" is incorrect because "am" is a present-tense auxiliary, whereas the given sentence is in the past tense.

• Option 2: "I were laugh at by Ramya" is incorrect because "were" does not agree with the singular subject "I" (which needs "was"), and "laugh" should be in its past participle form "laughed".

• Option 4: "I shall laugh at by Ramya" is incorrect because it uses the future auxiliary "shall" instead of the past auxiliary "was", and omits the past participle form altogether.

NOTE

• With phrasal/prepositional verbs like "laugh at", "look after", "listen to", the preposition must always be retained immediately after the past participle in the passive voice.

• Remember: the auxiliary "was" is used with singular subjects (I, he, she, it) and "were" with plural subjects (we, you, they) in the Simple Past passive.

question:
Comprehension:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

His only (1)________ was that he had no rifle. While running away from the village below, he had forgotten the rifle in a hurry. An unpardonable (2)________, but it was now too late to make amends for it. (3)________ he had the rifle, his pursuers would not have dared follow him with such brazen confidence. He would have hidden behind a rock and waited for them. As they came within his rifle’s range, he would have picked them off one by one. But now he could do (4)________ about it. He was unarmed. But come what may, he must (5)________ of their rifle’s range.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. regret.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage describes a man who fled without his rifle and now wishes things had been different — this sense of wishing something were otherwise is best expressed by "regret", meaning a feeling of sadness or disappointment over something that has happened or failed to happen.

• "His only regret was that he had no rifle" fits the context, since not having the rifle is precisely what troubles him, as confirmed by the next sentence describing it as "an unpardonable lapse".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "consolation" is incorrect because a consolation is something that offers comfort in a difficult situation — having no rifle is the opposite of comforting here.

• Option 3: "shock" is incorrect because "shock" denotes a sudden, surprising, and disturbing feeling, which does not fit the reflective tone of "his only ___ was that...".

• Option 4: "joy" is incorrect because it denotes happiness, which contradicts the clearly negative context of forgetting his rifle while fleeing.

NOTE

• In cloze passages, always read at least one sentence beyond the blank — here, the following sentence ("An unpardonable lapse...") confirms that the missing word must carry a negative, regretful sense.

• Words of similar sense to "regret": remorse, repentance, contrition — though these differ slightly in intensity and formality.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. lapse.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "lapse" is a brief or temporary failure of memory, concentration, judgement, etc.; a minor mistake or slip.

• The sentence "An unpardonable lapse, but it was now too late to make amends for it" fits perfectly — forgetting the rifle was a small but costly slip, and "to make amends for it" naturally follows from describing a mistake.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "yearn" is incorrect because it is a verb (meaning to long for something) and cannot function as the noun required by the sentence structure "An unpardonable ___".

• Option 3: "reward" is incorrect because a reward is something given in recognition of merit — this is a positive term that does not fit "unpardonable" or "make amends for it".

• Option 4: "crime" is incorrect because, although grammatically it could fit as a noun, forgetting a rifle in a hurry is not properly described as a "crime"; "lapse" is the far more precise and natural word for an unintentional slip.

NOTE

• The phrase "to make amends for" collocates naturally with mistakes/faults such as a lapse, an error, or a wrong, reinforcing why "lapse" is the best fit here.

• Related words: "slip", "oversight", "blunder" — all describe unintentional mistakes of varying severity.

question:
Comprehension:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

His only (1)________ was that he had no rifle. While running away from the village below, he had forgotten the rifle in a hurry. An unpardonable (2)________, but it was now too late to make amends for it. (3)________ he had the rifle, his pursuers would not have dared follow him with such brazen confidence. He would have hidden behind a rock and waited for them. As they came within his rifle’s range, he would have picked them off one by one. But now he could do (4)________ about it. He was unarmed. But come what may, he must (5)________ of their rifle’s range.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Had.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rule — Inverted (conditional) sentence, Type 3: When "if" is omitted from a Type 3 conditional clause (referring to an unreal/hypothetical past situation), the auxiliary "had" is placed at the very start of the clause, before the subject, in its place.
◦ Structure: Had + subject + past participle, ... + subject + would/could/might + have + past participle.

• The blank starts the sentence **"___ he had the rifle, his pursuers would not have dared follow him...", which is the inverted form of "If he had had the rifle, his pursuers would not have dared follow him...". The required word is therefore "Had"**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Has" is incorrect because it is a present-tense auxiliary and cannot begin an inverted Type 3 (past unreal) conditional clause.

• Option 3: "Have" is incorrect for the same reason — it does not carry the required past-tense/hypothetical sense.

• Option 4: "Did" is incorrect because inverted conditionals of this type require "had", not "did", to precede the subject and the past participle "had the rifle".

NOTE

• Inversion is also used with "Were" for Type 2 conditionals (e.g. "Were I you, I would...") and with "Should" for Type 1 conditionals (e.g. "Should it rain, we will cancel the trip").

• This inverted, "if"-less conditional style is common in formal/literary English and is frequently tested in SSC cloze passages.

solution_text:

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence reads **"But now he could do ___ about it. He was unarmed." Since he has no weapon, he is powerless to act — the most natural and idiomatic phrase is "could do nothing about it"**, meaning he was helpless to change or affect the situation.

• This is reinforced by the very next sentence, "He was unarmed", which explains exactly why he was helpless.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "anything" is incorrect because "could do anything about it" would suggest he was capable of acting, which contradicts "He was unarmed".

• Option 2: "something" is incorrect for the same reason — it implies some ability to act, which contradicts the context of helplessness.

• Option 3: "much" is incorrect because "could do much about it" would similarly imply some degree of capability, again contradicting his being unarmed and helpless.

NOTE

• The idiomatic phrase "could do nothing about it" is commonly used to express complete helplessness in a situation.

• Watch for supporting context clues in the surrounding sentences — here "He was unarmed" is the key clue confirming the negative sense of the blank.

solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. keep out.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrasal verb "keep out of" means to stay outside or beyond the boundary of something, especially to remain at a safe distance from danger.

• The sentence "he must keep out of their rifle’s range" means he must stay beyond the distance within which the pursuers' rifles could hit him — logically consistent with him being unarmed and needing to avoid danger.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "keep from" is incorrect because "keep from" means to refrain from doing something or to prevent something from happening — it does not combine naturally with "of their rifle’s range".

• Option 2: "keep within" is incorrect because it would mean staying inside the range (i.e., within reach of the pursuers' rifles), which is the opposite of the safety he needs to seek.

• Option 4: "keep of" is incorrect as it is not a valid English phrasal verb at all.

NOTE

• Common phrasal verbs with "keep" tested by SSC: keep up with (maintain pace), keep on (continue), keep away from (avoid), keep up (maintain), keep out of (stay outside/avoid).
